categories.label: Data quality risk
categories.description: Risk from fragmented, inconsistent or incomplete business data undermining AI output reliability
regulatory_refs: UK GDPR Article 5(1)(d) — data accuracy principle
fashion_extensions: Size and measurement data inconsistency across product lines prevents sizing AI from functioning reliably
Unstructured returns-reason data means Agent 2 recommendations for returns AI cannot be validated against real patterns

mitigations.HIGH: Conduct a full data audit before activating any Agent 2 executor outputs. Consolidate sales, inventory and customer records into one queryable system. Implement structured reason-code capture for all returns before deploying any customer-facing AI.
mitigations.MEDIUM: Establish data validation rules for all new product uploads and order processing. Schedule a quarterly data quality review.
mitigations.LOW: Maintain current data governance practices. Document data lineage for all AI-consumed datasets.

categories.label: Regulatory compliance risk
categories.description: Risk of non-compliance with UK data protection and AI governance obligations
regulatory_refs: UK GDPR 2018 — consent, data minimisation, subject access rights
Data (Use and Access) Act 2025 — data sharing obligations
UK AI Bill 2026 — transparency and human oversight requirements
fashion_extensions: Personalisation profiling requires explicit consent — not implied by purchase history alone under UK GDPR
Automated pricing decisions may require human review disclosure under the UK AI Bill 2026

mitigations.HIGH: Do not activate any Agent 2 executor output that touches customer data until privacy policy is updated to cover AI processing and explicit opt-in consent is documented. Register with ICO if not already done. Create a written staff AI use policy before any AI tool goes live.
mitigations.MEDIUM: Review privacy policy against UK GDPR AI processing requirements. Create a staff AI use policy. Monitor UK AI Bill 2026 guidance as it develops.
mitigations.LOW: Conduct an annual compliance review. Subscribe to ICO guidance updates.

categories.label: Staff adoption risk
categories.description: Risk that AI tools are rejected, misused or underutilised because staff lack confidence, skills or motivation
fashion_extensions: Longer-serving retail staff may resist AI-assisted product recommendations if they perceive it as undermining their styling expertise
Owner-manager resistance is the single strongest predictor of failed AI adoption in fashion SMEs

mitigations.HIGH: Identify one staff member as AI champion before any deployment. Run a structured two-hour onboarding session before go-live. Pilot with the most digitally confident team member first and use their experience to bring others along.
mitigations.MEDIUM: Provide role-specific guidance on how AI tools support rather than replace current tasks. Build a four-week settling-in period before evaluating adoption.
mitigations.LOW: Include AI tool updates in regular team meetings. Create a simple feedback channel for staff to flag issues.

categories.label: Vendor dependency risk
categories.description: Risk from reliance on a single AI provider, platform or tool including pricing changes, service discontinuation or lock-in
regulatory_refs: Data (Use and Access) Act 2025 — data portability provisions
fashion_extensions: Shopify platform dependency — significant portions of Agent 2 recommendations assume Shopify, creating risk if the business migrates platforms
Single marketing automation vendor lock-in — if Klaviyo is the only tool, all customer communication is at risk from a single vendor decision

mitigations.HIGH: Avoid building bespoke integrations to a single AI vendor before piloting. Ensure all AI-generated data is exportable in standard CSV format. Maintain a documented list of alternative providers for each tool deployed.
mitigations.MEDIUM: Test data export from each platform annually. Include vendor lock-in review in annual technology budget planning.
mitigations.LOW: Document alternative providers. Review vendor contracts annually.

categories.label: AI accuracy and hallucination risk
categories.description: Risk that LLM-generated outputs contain confident but incorrect information that damages customer trust or causes operational errors
regulatory_refs: UK AI Bill 2026 — accuracy and transparency obligations
Consumer Protection from Unfair Trading Regulations 2008 — misleading commercial practices
fashion_extensions: AI-generated size advice that is wrong drives returns rather than reducing them — directly counterproductive to the primary use case
AI-generated product descriptions containing incorrect material composition create trading standards liability

mitigations.HIGH: All AI-generated customer-facing content must pass through human review before publication. Use RAG-grounded outputs from Agent 2's knowledge base wherever possible rather than free-form generation. Implement a correction and logging process for identified AI errors.
mitigations.MEDIUM: Implement weekly spot-check audits of AI outputs. Create a clear customer escalation path for AI-related errors.
mitigations.LOW: Maintain a log of AI output corrections for continuous improvement.

categories.label: Ethical and bias risk
categories.description: Risk that AI systems perpetuate or amplify biases in product recommendations, sizing standards or customer targeting
regulatory_refs: UK Equality Act 2010 — protected characteristics in automated decision-making
UK AI Bill 2026 — fairness and non-discrimination provisions
fashion_extensions: Sizing bias — AI sizing recommendations trained primarily on standard UK size data may underserve plus-size, petite or non-standard body types who represent a majority of real customers
Fast-fashion sustainability — AI demand forecasting optimised purely for sell-through rate may conflict with the business's sustainability commitments or consumer expectations around overconsumption

mitigations.HIGH: Audit any sizing AI for performance across the full range of sizes stocked before customer-facing deployment. Document the data sources for any AI touching customer recommendations. Establish a human override mechanism for any AI-driven customer decision.
mitigations.MEDIUM: Include diversity and inclusion review in AI tool procurement. Test AI outputs for systematic bias across customer segments quarterly.
mitigations.LOW: Include ethical AI considerations in annual technology review.
